Rashi on Bava Metzia 81b:10:1.hebrew: דאי לאותובי רשותא בעי למישקל מיניה - וכי בתמיה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 81b:10:1.english: For if [he meant] to seat [him], does he require permission from him? - [This is stated] as a rhetorical question:

Rashi on Bava Metzia 81b:11:1.hebrew: ישבע - שלא פשע, דשומר חנם הוא עליו, דאין אדם נוטל משכונו לגוביינא אלא להיות בטוח במעותיו שלא יוכל הלווה לכפור, ולעולם שומר חנם הוא עליו, שאם אבד, יגבה ממקום אחר:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 81b:11:1.english: He takes an oath - that he was not negligent, because he is an unpaid bailee of it. For a person does not take his collateral for the purpose of collection, but only to be secure about his money, so that [the borrower] will not be able to deny [the debt]. And in all cases he is an unpaid bailee of it, so that if it was lost, he collects from elsewhere:

Rashi on Bava Metzia 81b:12:1.hebrew: אבל הלוהו אלף זוז בשטר והניח לו משכון עליהם דברי הכל אבדו מעותיו - דהא משכון ודאי לגוביינא שקל, לגבות הימנה, דסתם שטר יש בו שעבוד קרקעות, ויש לו מהיכן לגבות, ובטוח הוא, וגם לכפור אינו יכול, דהא קאי שטרא, הלכך לאו לזכרון דברים נקטיה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 81b:12:1.english: But if he lent him a thousand zuz by a promissory note and he left him collateral for them, according to everyone, [if the collateral is lost,] his money is lost - For the collateral was certainly taken for collection, to collect from it [if needed]. For an unspecified promissory note carries a lien on real property, and [the lender] has from where to collect, and he is secure; and [the borrower] also cannot deny [the debt], since the note stands [as evidence]. Therefore he did not take it as a reminder [of the debt]:

Rashi on Bava Metzia 81b:13:1.hebrew: כאן שמשכנו בשעת הלואתו - הברייתא קאמר כדעת ר' אליעזר דהוא שומר חנם. ומתני' מיירי כשמשכנו שלא בשעת הלואתו, אלא לאחר זמן, כשתבעו מעותיו בב"ד ולא שילם, ומשכנו על פי בית דין, דההוא ודאי לגוביינא שקליה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 81b:13:1.english: Here, [where] he took it as collateral at the time of his loan - [the baraita] speaks [in accordance with] Rabbi Eliezer, [who holds that he is] an unpaid bailee. And the mishna [speaks] of a case where he took the collateral not at the time of his loan, but after some time, when he demanded his money in court and [the borrower] did not pay, and he took the collateral by order of the court, for that [collateral] he certainly took for the sake of collection:

Rashi on Bava Metzia 81b:1:1.hebrew: עד דאתא אגניב - בלא פשיעה, וחייבינהו משום גניבה דשומר שכר:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 81b:1:1.english: Before he came, it was stolen - without negligence, and [Rav Pappa] deemed them liable on account of theft [which applies to] a paid guardian:

Rashi on Bava Metzia 81b:2:1.hebrew: סדינא - של פשתן, ואין מים מכבידין אותו כל כך:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 81b:2:1.english: Sheet - [It was] made of linen, and water does not weigh it down so much:

Rashi on Bava Metzia 81b:2:2.hebrew: סרבלא - גלופקרא היא בגד שקורין קו"ץ, והוא של צמר, והרבה מים נבלעין בו ומכבידין אותו. לפיכך פשט הנמוך הסרבל ונתכסה בסדין:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 81b:2:2.english: Sarbela - [It is] a galofkara, which [in Old French] is called cou"ts, and it is made of wool, and a lot of water is absorbed in it and weighs it down. Therefore, [the short one] removed the cloak and covered himself with the sheet:

Rashi on Bava Metzia 81b:3:1.hebrew: שאלה בבעלים היא - שבשעת השאלה היה המשאיל במלאכתו של שואל, ונשא סרבל שלו על חמורו, ומעביר לו על אמת המים:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 81b:3:1.english: It is borrowing with the owners - For at the time of the borrowing, the lender was engaged in the borrower's work, and carried his [the borrower's] cloak on his donkey, and was transporting it for him across the water channel:

Rashi on Bava Metzia 81b:5:1.hebrew: במקום עדים - דאנן סהדי שאין אותו הדרך בלא מים:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 81b:5:1.english: In a place of witnesses - for we ourselves are witnesses that this road is not without water:

Rashi on Bava Metzia 81b:6:1.hebrew: הנח לפניך אינו לא שומר חנם כו' - כיון דאמר ליה "לפניך", תיב ונטר לך קא"ל:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 81b:6:1.english: [If he said,] "Place [it] before yourself," he is neither an unpaid bailee etc. - Since he said to him "before yourself," he was saying to him: "Sit and guard [it] for yourself."

Rashi on Bava Metzia 81b:8:1.hebrew: לימא - מתניתין הני דקתני סתמא, תנאי היא:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 81b:8:1.english: Let us say - [In the case of] these [items in our mishna], which [the mishna] states without specification, it is [a matter of dispute] between tanna'im:

Rashi on Bava Metzia 81b:8:2.hebrew: אם הכניס ברשות - משנה היא בפרק שור שנגח את הפרה (ב"ק ד' מז.), בקדר שהכניס קדירותיו, ושברן שורו של בעל הבית, או הכניס שורו, ונגחו שורו של בעל הבית, או שהכניס פירותיו, ואכלתו בהמתו:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 81b:8:2.english: If he brought [his items] in with permission - This is a mishna in the chapter [entitled] "An ox that gored a cow" (Bava Kamma, page 47a), [dealing] with a potter who brought in his pots, and the ox of the homeowner broke them; or he brought in his ox, and the ox of the homeowner gored it; or he brought in his produce, and [the homeowner's] animal ate it:

Rashi on Bava Metzia 81b:8:3.hebrew: בעל חצר חייב - בנזקו, דכי אמר ליה בעל החצר: "עול, עול, ואנטר לך" קאמר ליה, וה"ה אם הנח סתמא בשוק:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 81b:8:3.english: The owner of the courtyard is liable - for the damage [the items sustain], because when [the owner of the courtyard] said to him, "Enter, enter, and I will guard for you," he is saying [this to him]. And the same applies [if] he placed [his items] without specification in the marketplace.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 81b:8:4.hebrew: רבי אומר בכולן אינו חייב - דעול ותיב ונטר לך קאמר ליה, וה"ה אם אמר להנח סתמא בשוק:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 81b:8:4.english: Rabbi says: In all [cases] he is not liable - [This is] because [the owner of the items] is saying to him, "Go in, sit, and guard for yourself," [meaning that the owner of the courtyard is not responsible for the items]; and the same applies [if the owner of the items] placed [them] without specification in the marketplace:

Rashi on Bava Metzia 81b:9:1.hebrew: דבת נטורי היא - שאין אדם מכניס דבר לתוכה אלא להשתמר בה, דאין טורח בשמירתה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 81b:9:1.english: It is a place that can be safeguarded - For a person only brings an item into it in order that it be guarded there, as there is no effort involved in guarding it:

Rashi on Bava Metzia 81b:9:2.hebrew: עול דאינטר לך קאמר ליה - שאין שמירה קשה עלי:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 81b:9:2.english: "Enter, so that I may guard for you," he said to him - for guarding is not burdensome for me:

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 81b:12:1.hebrew: דברי הכל אבד המשכון אבדו מעותיו - פירוש: לכך מודה רבי אליעזר משום דהוי שלא בשעת הלואתו, וקני משכון. ושטר דנקט לאו דוקא, אלא לומר דאיירי שלא בשעת הלואתו, דכיון שעשה שטר, מסתמא לא לקח משכון בשעת הלואה [עד] אחרי כן. אבל רישא דפליגי, היינו בשעת הלואה. ולמאי דמוקי לה דפליגי בדרבי יצחק, היה סבור דרבי יצחק איירי אף בשעת הלואה, ורבי אליעזר פליג עליה בהא, אבל בסיפא דאיירי שלא בשעת הלואה מודה דקני, דעיקר קרא דולך תהיה צדקה איירי שלא בשעת הלואה. ועל פ"ה דפי' שלהי שבועת הדיינים (שבועות ד' מד. ושם ד"ה מאי) דמשום שטר מודה ר' אליעזר בסיפא, דכיון דיש שטר, לשם משכון קבל, ולא לזכרון דברים בעלמא כמו ברישא - תימה! דאי ברישא לא נקט משכון אלא לזכרון דברים בעלמא משום דליכא שטרא, א"כ אמאי לא יהיה משמט אפילו שוה המשכון כנגד מעותיו, כדמשמע בהזהב (לעיל בבא מציעא מט.) דהיכא דלא נקט אלא לזכרון דברים בעלמא דמשמט; והתם משמע דאם שוה משכון כנגד מעותיו, לכ"ע אינו משמט. ועוד, אמאי קאמר מתניתין מחוורתא דלא כרבי אליעזר? לוקמה בשטר דמודה ר' אליעזר! אלא ש"מ דאף ר' אליעזר אינו מודה אלא שלא בשעת הלואה. ומיהו יש לתרץ, דהלוהו על המשכון משמע בלא שטר. ועוד, דאי מתני' מיירי בשטר, לא הוה פליג ר' יהודה דאמר הלוהו מעות שומר חנם, דלא יחלוק ארבי אליעזר ורבי עקיבא. ובה"ג דרב יהודאי גאון נמי משמע דסיפא דהלוהו בשטר איירי שלא בשעת הלואה, דמוקי הא דאמר רבי יצחק דב"ח קונה משכון, היינו דוקא שלא בשעת הלואה, אבל בשעת הלואה לא קני - היינו דוקא בשטר, דכיון דאיכא שטרא, לא סמיך אמשכון אלא אשטרא; אבל בלא שטר, אפילו בשעת הלואה קני, והוי שומר שכר. ושלא בשעת הלואה הוי שומר שכר, אע"ג דאיכא שטרא, דודאי אמשכון סמיך. וא"כ סיפא דהלוהו בשטר איירי שלא בשעת הלואה, דבשעת הלואה לא איבד מעותיו, דאשטר סמיך. ומה שר"ל דהיכא דליכא שטר קני אפילו בשעת הלואה, לא מטעם דר' יצחק, דקרא לא איירי אלא שלא בשעת הלואה, אלא קני מדשמואל, וסברי דהלכה כשמואל ואין הלכה כרב יוסף:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 81b:12:1.english: Everyone agrees: if the collateral is lost, his money is lost - Meaning: Rabbi Eliezer agrees for this reason, because it was not at the time of the loan, and [the lender] acquires the collateral. And the note [the Mishnah] mentioned is not meant precisely, but rather to say that it is speaking of [collateral taken] not at the time of the loan; for since he made a note, presumably he did not take collateral at the time of the loan, [but only] afterward. But in the first clause, where they dispute, [the case] is at the time of the loan. And according to [the Gemara's] explanation that they dispute the matter of Rabbi Yitzchak, [the Gemara] thought that Rabbi Yitzchak was speaking even of [collateral taken] at the time of the loan, and Rabbi Eliezer disagrees with him in this; but in the latter clause, which speaks of not at the time of the loan, he agrees that [the lender] acquires, because the main [application of] the verse "and it shall be righteousness for you" is [where the collateral is taken] not at the time of the loan. Now, regarding the explanation of Rashi at the end of [chapter] Shevuat HaDayanim (Shevuot 44a, s.v. "Mai"), that Rabbi Eliezer agrees in the latter clause because of the note — since there is a note, he took [the collateral] for the sake of collateral, and not as a mere reminder, as in the first clause — this is astonishing! For if in the first clause he took collateral only as a mere reminder because there is no note, then why should [the debt] not be released [by the Sabbatical year] even where the collateral is worth as much as his money, as is implied in [the chapter] HaZahav (above, Bava Metzia 49a), that where he took [it] only as a mere reminder, [the debt] is released; and there it implies that if the collateral is worth as much as his money, everyone agrees [the debt] is not released. Furthermore, why does the Mishnah say "it is clear that it is not like Rabbi Eliezer"? Let it establish [the Mishnah] as [dealing] with a note, where Rabbi Eliezer agrees! Rather, learn from this that even Rabbi Eliezer agrees only [where the collateral was taken] not at the time of the loan. However, one can answer that "he lent him on the collateral" implies without a note. Furthermore, if the Mishnah were speaking of a note, Rabbi Yehuda, who said [that if] he lent him money [the lender is] an unpaid custodian, would not [be understood to] disagree with Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Akiva. And in the Halakhot Gedolot of Rav Yehudai Gaon too, it is implied that the latter clause, "he lent him with a note," speaks of not at the time of the loan; for he establishes that which Rabbi Yitzchak said, that a creditor acquires collateral, as meaning specifically not at the time of the loan, but at the time of the loan he does not acquire — [and that] this is specifically with a note, since when there is a note, he does not rely on the collateral but on the note; but without a note, even at the time of the loan he acquires, and he is a paid custodian. And not at the time of the loan he is a paid custodian even though there is a note, for certainly he relies on the collateral. And if so, the latter clause, "he lent him with a note," speaks of not at the time of the loan, [for] at the time of the loan he did not lose his money, since he relied on the note. And as for that which he said, that where there is no note he acquires even at the time of the loan — [this is] not by virtue of Rabbi Yitzchak, since the verse speaks only of not at the time of the loan, but rather he acquires [it] from [the view of] Shmuel; and they hold that the halakha follows Shmuel and not Rav Yosef:

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 81b:14:1.hebrew: והא אידי ואידי הלוהו על המשכון קתני - משמע דמלוה חבירו על המשכון משמע בשעת הלואה. ותימה, דבפרק השולח (גיטין לז. ושם ד"ה שאני) קאמר: תנן, המלוה את חבירו על המשכון והמוסר שטרותיו לב"ד אינו משמט, ומפ' התם דהמלוה על המשכון אינו משמט משום דקני ליה מדר' יצחק, והא לא קאמר רבי יצחק אלא שלא בשעת הלואתו, ו"על המשכון" משמע דאפילו בשעת הלואתו אינו משמט! ויש לומר, דכיון שלא בשעת הלואה קני ליה לגמרי מדרבי יצחק, בשעת הלואה נמי, דליכא קנין, אלא שעבוד אלים שעבודיה ליחשב "ולא של אחיך בידך". וכן בפרק כל שעה (פסחים ד' לא: ושם ד"ה בדר"י) גבי ישראל שהלוה לנכרי על חמצו, עובר עליו משום דרבי יצחק, כדאמרינן התם. התם נמי, כיון דשלא בשעת הלואה קני, אהני שעבודיה בשעת הלואה ליחשב כשל ישראל. וכן נכרי שהלוה לישראל על חמצו, אי לאו דנכרי מישראל לא קני, לא היה נאסר אף משכנו בשעת הלואתו דלא קני; כיון דשלא בשעת הלואה הוה קני, בשעת הלואה נמי הוה אלים שעבודיה דנכרי, שלא יצטרך לבערו. ואף על גב דהוי דישראל, וקרינא ביה "שלך", מ"מ מדאפקיה קרא "מלא ימצא", לא מחייב אלא כשמצוי לו לגמרי, וכיון דאלים שעבודיה דנכרי, לא חשיב מצוי. והכי נמי אמרינן בפרק קמא דפסחים (ד' ו. ושם ד"ה יחד): יחד לו בית, אין זקוק לבער, אע"ג דחשיב לגמרי כשל ישראל כיון דקבל אחריות, מ"מ כיון דיחד לו בית, אינו מצוי אצלו:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 81b:14:1.english: But don't both this and that teach "he lent him against a pledge" - This implies that "one who lends his fellow against a pledge" means at the time of the loan. And this is surprising, for in the chapter [entitled] Hashole'ach (Gittin 37a, and see there s.v. Sheni) [the Gemara] says: We learned [in a mishna]: One who lends his fellow against a pledge, and one who hands over his promissory notes to the court, [the Sabbatical year] does not cancel [the debt]. And [the Gemara] explains there that one who lends against a pledge is not canceled because he has acquired it, based on [the view of] Rabbi Yitzchak. But Rabbi Yitzchak only said [this] when [the pledge is taken] not at the time of the loan, whereas "against a pledge" implies that even at the time of the loan it does not cancel! And one can say: Since [when taken] not at the time of the loan he acquires it entirely, based on Rabbi Yitzchak, at the time of the loan too, [even though] there is no acquisition, [there is] a strong lien, [and the] lien is strong enough to be considered [as meaning] "and not that of your brother [shall be] in your hand." And likewise in the chapter [entitled] Kol Sha'ah (Pesachim 31b, and see there s.v. Bedar'i), regarding a Jew who lent money to a gentile against his chametz, he transgresses [the prohibition] regarding it because of Rabbi Yitzchak, as [the Gemara] says there. There too, since [when taken] not at the time of the loan he acquires it, his lien at the time of the loan serves to be considered as belonging to the Jew. And likewise, [regarding] a gentile who lent to a Jew against his chametz: if not for the fact that a gentile does not acquire [a pledge] from a Jew, it would not be prohibited — even his pledge at the time of the loan, in which he does not acquire it; since [when taken] not at the time of the loan he would acquire it, at the time of the loan too the gentile's lien is strong, so that [the Jew] need not remove it. And even though it belongs to the Jew and we apply to it [the term] "yours," nevertheless, since the verse excluded it with [the phrase] "shall not be found," he is liable only when it is entirely available to him, and since the gentile's lien is strong, it is not considered available. And so too [the Gemara] says in the first chapter of Pesachim (6a, and see there s.v. Yachad): If he designated a house for him, he is not obligated to remove [the chametz], even though it is considered entirely as belonging to the Jew since he accepted responsibility; nevertheless, since he designated a house for him, it is not available to him:
